newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end up in flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end up in flat trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished slightly higher on Tuesday in light trade with the market seen drifting in the absence of fresh buying in the market, dealers said.
"The prices were steady, but it was flat all around and very quiet. There simply was no substantial business to pick up the market the whole day," a local rubber trader said.
Japan failed to provide any inspiration for the market after Tokyo's March contract ended unchanged at 133.0 yen while Kobe's March contract settled at 132.6, up 0.2 yen from yesterday's settlement.
"Japan's prices went up only very slightly. If it had increased by limit-up, then it would have moved the market here," another trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 123.00-124.00 U.S. cents a kg from 122.75 cents.
November RSS1 was seen at 175.00-176.00 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.25) a kg from yesterday's settlement of 174.75 cents.
December TSR20 was seen at 172.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.24) a kg against the previous 173.25 cents.
